item_identification.note: The leaf's subject is a 'Time Stop' item. The cached catalogue contains exactly two items whose active is named 'Time Stop': Zhonya's Hourglass (3157) and Seeker's Armguard (2420). Wooglet's Witchcap (228002) carries the same stasis active under the name 'Stasis' and is not a Summoner's Rift item (modes['classic sr 5v5'] = false). The computation below holds identically for both Time Stop items, so the verdict does not depend on which index [1] resolves to.

step_1_what_the_item_actually_declares.finding: The new reason asserts 'Every declared family on this item is a defence.' The cached atom decomposition declares three distinct families, and at most one of them (crowd-control-mobility.stasis) is defensive in character. The 'stats' family carries 105 flat Ability Power (40 on Seeker's Armguard) - a strictly offensive stat that raises outgoing damage on every AP-ratio hit - and the fourth atom is literally in the 'damage' family (damage.resistance-mitigation, related to damage.damage-instance / armor-penetration / magic-penetration). The universal claim is therefore false on the cached data: not every declared family is a defence, and the item's offensive stat family is the largest single component of its 3250g cost.

step_2_does_stasis_leave_outgoing_TDD_un.source_a: data/items.json -> 3157.active[0] 'Time Stop' branches[0] (verbatim): "Put yourself in {{tip|stasis (buff)|stasis}} for {{fd|2.5}} seconds, rendering you {{tip|untargetable}} and {{tip|invulnerable}} for the duration but also unable to move, declare [[basic attack]]s, cast [[champion ability|abilities]], use [[summoner spell]]s, or [[active ability items|activate items]]."
step_2_does_stasis_leave_outgoing_TDD_un.source_b: data/wiki-atoms/crowd-control-mobility.json -> crowd-control-mobility.stasis description (verbatim): "Full disable that also makes the unit invulnerable and untargetable; cannot be cleansed, unaffected by tenacity, disables even summoner spells."
step_2_does_stasis_leave_outgoing_TDD_un.source_c: data/items.json -> 3157.simpleDescription (verbatim): "Activate to become invincible but unable to take actions"
step_2_does_stasis_leave_outgoing_TDD_un.derivation: Let W be the fight window in seconds and let d = 2.5 s of stasis be taken inside W. During d the wielder can neither declare basic attacks nor cast abilities (explicit in the cached wiki branch text and in the stasis atom's 'full disable' definition). Total damage dealt over a fixed window is the integral of output over the window; stasis zeroes output on a sub-interval of positive measure d = 2.5 s. Hence TDD(with stasis) = TDD(W - 2.5 s of active output) < TDD(W) whenever any output would have landed in that interval. Stasis is a two-sided mechanic: it changes durability (invulnerable/untargetable) AND it strictly reduces outgoing damage over a fixed window.
step_2_does_stasis_leave_outgoing_TDD_un.finding: The new reason's second clause - 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD' - is contradicted verbatim by the cached wiki text, which spells out that the wielder is 'unable to ... declare basic attacks, cast abilities'. Zero output for 2.5 s is an outgoing-TDD change, not a durability-only change.

step_3_is_the_old_reason_consistent_with.claim_a: 'Time Stop is priced only from the explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input.'
step_3_is_the_old_reason_consistent_with.check_a: The cached entry places Time Stop under 'active' (data/items.json -> 3157.active), not under 'passives' (3157.passives == []). An active must be cast to take effect, and its effect is time-boxed at a fixed, wiki-bounded {{fd|2.5}} seconds per cast; riotDescription corroborates: 'Enter Stasis for 2.5 seconds.' A quantity of stasis seconds is therefore an input to the fight, bounded by the source-stated 2.5 s per activation, not something derivable from the item entry alone.
step_3_is_the_old_reason_consistent_with.check_b: Consistent with the same evidence: passives == [] means nothing about this item fires without an activation, and no cached field states an automatic or on-death trigger (contrast 3026 Guardian Angel, whose 'Rebirth' is a passive and does fire without input). Assuming stasis merely from ownership would invent an unsourced cast.
step_3_is_the_old_reason_consistent_with.finding: Both clauses of the old reason are supported by the cached source; neither overstates it.

step_4_docs_check.result: The document states the identities for the engine's core families (resistance mitigation m(R)=100/(100+R), renewal-process cast counting 'a cast counts when it starts within the window' (line 62), DoT partitioning, revive as an absorbing-state machine). It contains no formula that prices stasis and no statement that a stasis window is durability-only. The window-based accounting it does state (output counted by events landing inside the fight window) is what makes the step-2 derivation bite: an interval in which no cast can start contributes no damage events.

conclusion: The new value fails on two independently sufficient grounds: (1) the cached atom decomposition declares a 'stats' family carrying 105 AP and a 'damage' family, so 'every declared family on this item is a defence' is false; (2) the cached wiki text for Time Stop explicitly disables basic attacks and abilities for 2.5 s, so the mechanic demonstrably reduces outgoing damage over a fixed window and 'changes durability, not outgoing TDD' is false. The old value is fully consistent with the cached source: Time Stop is an active with a source-bounded 2.5 s duration, the item has no passives, and nothing in the cached entry makes stasis occur without an explicit cast.
